summary: When items bulk-set --apply stops early on an exhausted 429, it must persist which item IDs it already wrote (keyed by a signature of collection + --match + --set) so a re-run of the identical command skips those and reaches the untouched tail, instead of reselecting the same sorted head of the batch from the unchanged local mirror.
reason: The local mirror this command selects from is opened read-only and is never updated after a write, so a bare re-run after a rate-limit stop reselects the exact same sorted matched list from scratch. Without tracking what was already applied, the re-run burns rate-limit budget resending writes to items that already succeeded and can make zero net forward progress on the remaining items if the per-minute cap is tight enough. The fix adds a small sidecar JSON file under the CLI's state dir (mirrors the teach command's existing pattern of a state-dir sidecar file) recording applied item IDs per signature; it is cleared whenever a run for that signature finishes without hitting the rate limit. A regen must keep the 'Re-run to continue where this left off' message backed by this resume state rather than reverting to a message that promises continuation the tool can't deliver.
validated_outcome: Unit tests TestBulkSetResumeRoundTrip and TestBulkSetResumeClearIgnoresOtherSignature confirm save/load/clear round-trips correctly and that finishing one --match/--set batch never wipes a different in-flight batch's resume state on the same collection.
